🧠 Project Description

This project builds a movie recommendation system that goes beyond simple collaborative filtering by incorporating a time-decay factor into user profiles. The idea is that a user's recent ratings are more indicative of their current preferences than older ratings. It utilizes pandas for data loading and manipulation of user-item interaction data (e.g., MovieLens dataset). The Surprise library is employed for its efficient implementation of various recommendation algorithms (like SVD or KNN). However, the core innovation here involves creating time-weighted user profiles. This is achieved by calculating weighted average ratings or feature vectors for users, giving higher weight to recent interactions. These time-aware user profiles are then used with item profiles (e.g., based on genres) to generate recommendations, often using techniques like Cosine Similarity to find items similar to the user's current weighted preferences.

🧪 Example Input & Output

Input:

  • User-item interaction data (e.g., MovieLens dataset): UserID, MovieID, Rating, Timestamp.
  • Movie metadata (optional but helpful): MovieID, Title, Genres.
  • Target UserID for recommendations.
  • Number of recommendations desired (e.g., top 10).
  • Time-decay parameter (e.g., half-life in days).

Expected Output:

  • A ranked list of MovieIDs (and optionally Titles/Genres) recommended for the target user, reflecting their time-weighted preferences.
  • (Optional) The calculated time-weighted profile vector for the target user.
  • (Optional) Evaluation metrics if comparing different decay functions or recommendation approaches (e.g., Precision@k, Recall@k).

🧰 Frameworks & Libraries Used

  • pandas: For loading, manipulating, and time-based weighting of rating data.
  • numpy: For numerical calculations, especially for weighting and vector operations.
  • scikit-learn: For TfidfVectorizer (if using genre-based item profiles) and cosine_similarity.
  • surprise: (Optional, can be used alongside or as an alternative) For standard recommendation algorithms and data handling (Reader, Dataset). The time-decay logic might be implemented separately or by customizing Surprise algorithms if possible.
  • datetime, time: For handling timestamps and calculating time differences for decay.

🧾 Final Product Output

  • A Python script (movie_recommendation_engine_time_decay.py) implementing the data loading, time-weighted profile creation, similarity calculation, and recommendation generation.
  • A function or class that takes a UserID and returns a list of recommended MovieIDs.
  • (Optional) Saved user/item profile vectors if pre-calculated.

🔁 Where to Go From Here

  • Experiment with different time-decay functions (exponential, linear, etc.) and parameters.
  • Incorporate item-based features (genres, actors, directors) more deeply into the profiling using techniques like TF-IDF or embeddings.
  • Combine the time-weighted approach with matrix factorization methods (like SVD from Surprise) for hybrid recommendations.
  • Develop a more sophisticated user profile that captures evolving interests beyond simple weighted averages.
  • Build an API or simple web interface to serve recommendations.
  • Evaluate the impact of time decay on recommendation quality using appropriate offline metrics and potentially A/B testing.
  • Handle the cold-start problem for new users or items using content-based or hybrid approaches.

Now, let's proceed with the implementation (using MovieLens 100k dataset and focusing on time-weighted profile similarity).

# movie_recommendation_engine_time_decay.py

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from sklearn.feature_extraction.text import TfidfVectorizer
from sklearn.metrics.pairwise import cosine_similarity
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
import time
import math

# --- Configuration ---
# Using MovieLens 100k data paths (adjust if needed)
RATINGS_FILE: str = "ml-100k/u.data"
ITEMS_FILE: str = "ml-100k/u.item"
SEPARATOR: str = "\t"
TOP_N_RECOMMENDATIONS: int = 10
# Time Decay Parameters
DECAY_FUNCTION_TYPE: str = "exponential" # Options: "exponential", "linear", "none"
HALF_LIFE_DAYS: float = 60 # For exponential decay: time for weight to reduce by half
MAX_AGE_DAYS: float = 365 # For linear decay: ratings older than this get zero weight
REFERENCE_TIMESTAMP: int = int(time.time()) # Use current time as reference for decay

# --- Data Loading ---
def load_movielens_100k(ratings_path: str, items_path: str, sep: str) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Loads MovieLens 100k ratings and item data."""
    try:
        print("Loading MovieLens 100k data...")
        # Ratings: user_id, item_id, rating, timestamp
        r_cols = ["user_id", "movie_id", "rating", "unix_timestamp"]
        ratings = pd.read_csv(ratings_path, sep=sep, names=r_cols, encoding="latin-1")
        ratings["timestamp"] = pd.to_datetime(ratings["unix_timestamp"], unit="s")

        # Items: movie_id, title, release_date, ..., genres (binary columns)
        i_cols = ["movie_id", "title", "release_date", "video_release_date", "imdb_url"] + \
                 ["genre_unknown", "Action", "Adventure", "Animation", "Children\\'s", "Comedy",
                  "Crime", "Documentary", "Drama", "Fantasy", "Film-Noir", "Horror",
                  "Musical", "Mystery", "Romance", "Sci-Fi", "Thriller", "War", "Western"]
        items = pd.read_csv(items_path, sep="|", names=i_cols, encoding="latin-1")

        # Create a single 'genres' string column for easier processing
        genre_cols = items.columns[-19:] # Last 19 columns are genres
        items["genres_str"] = items[genre_cols].apply(lambda row: "|".join(row.index[row == 1]), axis=1)

        print(f"Ratings loaded: {ratings.shape}")
        print(f"Items loaded: {items.shape}")
        return ratings, items[["movie_id", "title", "genres_str"]]
    except FileNotFoundError:
        print(f"Error: MovieLens data files not found at expected paths ({ratings_path}, {items_path}).")
        print("Please download the MovieLens 100k dataset and place the u.data and u.item files correctly.")
        exit()
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"An error occurred during data loading: {e}")
        exit()

# --- Item Profile Creation (TF-IDF on Genres) ---
def create_item_profiles(items: pd.DataFrame) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, TfidfVectorizer, np.ndarray]:
    """Creates item profiles using TF-IDF on genres."""
    print("Creating item profiles using TF-IDF on genres...")
    # Replace missing genres string with empty string
    items["genres_str"] = items["genres_str"].fillna("")

    tfidf = TfidfVectorizer(token_pattern="[^|]+") # Split by pipe
    tfidf_matrix = tfidf.fit_transform(items["genres_str"])

    # Store TF-IDF vectors with movie_id
    item_profiles = pd.DataFrame(tfidf_matrix.toarray(), index=items["movie_id"], columns=tfidf.get_feature_names_out())
    print(f"Item profiles created. Shape: {item_profiles.shape}")
    return item_profiles, tfidf, tfidf_matrix

# --- Time Decay Weighting ---
def calculate_time_weight(timestamp: pd.Timestamp, ref_timestamp: int, decay_type: str, half_life_days: float, max_age_days: float) -> float:
    """Calculates the weight for a rating based on its age and decay type."""
    age_seconds: float = ref_timestamp - timestamp.timestamp()
    age_days: float = age_seconds / (60 * 60 * 24)

    if age_days < 0: age_days = 0 # Handle potential future timestamps

    if decay_type == "exponential":
        # w = exp(-lambda * t), where lambda = ln(2) / half_life
        if half_life_days <= 0:
            return 1.0 # No decay if half-life is non-positive
        decay_rate = math.log(2) / half_life_days
        weight = math.exp(-decay_rate * age_days)
    elif decay_type == "linear":
        if max_age_days <= 0:
            return 1.0 # No decay if max_age is non-positive
        weight = max(0.0, 1.0 - (age_days / max_age_days))
    elif decay_type == "none":
        weight = 1.0
    else:
        print(f"Warning: Unknown decay_type     '{decay_type}   '. Using no decay.")
        weight = 1.0

    return weight

# --- User Profile Creation (Time-Weighted) ---
def create_time_weighted_user_profile(user_id: int, user_ratings: pd.DataFrame, item_profiles: pd.DataFrame, ref_timestamp: int, decay_type: str, half_life: float, max_age: float) -> np.ndarray:
    """Creates a time-weighted profile for a single user."""
    if user_ratings.empty:
        # Return zero vector if user has no ratings
        return np.zeros(item_profiles.shape[1])

    # Calculate weights for each rating
    user_ratings["time_weight"] = user_ratings["timestamp"].apply(
        lambda ts: calculate_time_weight(ts, ref_timestamp, decay_type, half_life, max_age)
    )

    # Get profiles of items rated by the user
    rated_item_ids = user_ratings["movie_id"].tolist()
    rated_item_profiles = item_profiles.loc[item_profiles.index.isin(rated_item_ids)]

    # Align ratings and profiles (important if some items lack profiles)
    aligned_ratings = user_ratings.set_index("movie_id").loc[rated_item_profiles.index]

    # Calculate weighted average profile
    # Weight = time_weight * (rating - average_rating) - optional mean centering
    # Simpler: Weight = time_weight * rating
    weights = aligned_ratings["time_weight"] * aligned_ratings["rating"]
    weighted_profiles = rated_item_profiles.multiply(weights, axis=0)

    # Sum weighted profiles and normalize (optional, helps with cosine similarity)
    user_profile_vec = weighted_profiles.sum(axis=0)
    norm = np.linalg.norm(user_profile_vec)
    if norm > 0:
        user_profile_vec /= norm

    return user_profile_vec.values # Return as numpy array

# --- Recommendation Generation ---
def generate_recommendations(user_id: int, user_profile_vec: np.ndarray, item_profiles: pd.DataFrame, all_ratings: pd.DataFrame, top_n: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Generates top N recommendations based on cosine similarity."""
    if np.all(user_profile_vec == 0):
        print(f"User {user_id} has a zero profile vector (no ratings or all weights zero). Cannot recommend.")
        return pd.DataFrame(columns=["movie_id", "similarity_score"])

    # Calculate cosine similarity between user profile and all item profiles
    # Reshape user_profile_vec for sklearn's cosine_similarity function
    user_profile_reshaped = user_profile_vec.reshape(1, -1)
    similarities = cosine_similarity(user_profile_reshaped, item_profiles.values)[0] # Get the first (only) row

    # Create DataFrame of similarities
    sim_df = pd.DataFrame({"movie_id": item_profiles.index, "similarity_score": similarities})

    # Filter out movies already rated by the user
    rated_movies = all_ratings[all_ratings["user_id"] == user_id]["movie_id"].unique()
    sim_df_filtered = sim_df[~sim_df["movie_id"].isin(rated_movies)]

    # Get top N recommendations
    recommendations = sim_df_filtered.sort_values(by="similarity_score", ascending=False).head(top_n)

    return recommendations

# --- Main Execution ---
if __name__ == "__main__":
    # 1. Load Data
    ratings_df, items_df = load_movielens_100k(RATINGS_FILE, ITEMS_FILE, SEPARATOR)

    # 2. Create Item Profiles
    item_profiles_df, _, _ = create_item_profiles(items_df)

    # 3. Select Target User and Get Their Ratings
    target_user_id: int = 196 # Example user ID
    user_ratings_df = ratings_df[ratings_df["user_id"] == target_user_id].copy()

    if user_ratings_df.empty:
        print(f"Error: Target user {target_user_id} not found or has no ratings.")
    else:
        print(f"\nGenerating recommendations for User ID: {target_user_id}")
        print(f"Using time decay: type=    '{DECAY_FUNCTION_TYPE}  ', half_life={HALF_LIFE_DAYS} days, max_age={MAX_AGE_DAYS} days")

        # 4. Create Time-Weighted User Profile
        user_profile_vector: np.ndarray = create_time_weighted_user_profile(
            target_user_id,
            user_ratings_df,
            item_profiles_df,
            REFERENCE_TIMESTAMP,
            DECAY_FUNCTION_TYPE,
            HALF_LIFE_DAYS,
            MAX_AGE_DAYS
        )

        # 5. Generate Recommendations
        recommendations_df: pd.DataFrame = generate_recommendations(
            target_user_id,
            user_profile_vector,
            item_profiles_df,
            ratings_df, # Pass all ratings to filter out watched items
            TOP_N_RECOMMENDATIONS
        )

        # 6. Display Results
        if not recommendations_df.empty:
            print(f"\nTop {TOP_N_RECOMMENDATIONS} Recommendations for User {target_user_id}:")
            # Merge with item titles for readability
            recommendations_with_titles = pd.merge(
                recommendations_df,
                items_df[["movie_id", "title", "genres_str"]],
                on="movie_id",
                how="left"
            )
            print(recommendations_with_titles[["movie_id", "title", "genres_str", "similarity_score"]].to_string(index=False))
        else:
            print("No recommendations could be generated.")

    print("\n--- Project Execution Finished ---")

This implementation demonstrates building a movie recommendation engine that incorporates time decay into user profiles. It loads MovieLens data, creates item profiles based on genres using TF-IDF, calculates time-weighted user profiles giving more importance to recent ratings, and then uses cosine similarity between the user profile and item profiles to generate personalized recommendations, excluding movies the user has already rated.
